editorial:
Imagine waking up to news that a random shooter is picking people off in broad daylight, and nobody knows who or where they are. That is exactly the nightmare you get into with this movie. It takes you right into the heart of the 2002 sniper attacks, showing the sheer panic as people are terrified to even go to a gas station. You will see the police and FBI scrambling to find a lead, but they keep chasing a white van that turns out to be a dead end. Meanwhile, the actual killers are hiding in plain sight, watching the chaos they caused with a cold, creepy smile. It feels like a ticking clock where the tension just keeps building up.

What really works here is how it shows the frustration of the investigators and the fear of the public. The acting is solid and keeps you glued to your seat, though some parts feel a bit like an old TV movie. If you like true crime stories that make you feel uneasy, you will love this. Since it is an older flick, you might want to look for a remastered version to rent on Apple TV or grab the Blu-ray for your physical collection to get the best picture quality. It is a great pick for a rainy weekend if you want something that feels real and scary.
endingExplained: The movie ends when the police finally stop chasing the wrong leads and get a real tip about the killers. They track down John Allen Muhammad and his grandson, Lee Boyd Leeper, who were hiding in a blue car. The police surround the vehicle and arrest them both. You find out the shocker was that the sniper was firing from inside the car's trunk, which is why the police missed them for so long.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves true crime and police procedurals.
